question:
An NPN transistor is used in a CE amplifier with voltage-divider bias:

- $V_{CC}=12\,\text{V}$
- $R_C=2.2\,\text{k}\Omega$
- $R_E=1.0\,\text{k}\Omega$ (bypassed by a large capacitor for AC, so emitter is AC-grounded)
- Bias resistors: $R_1=100\,\text{k}\Omega$ (from $V_{CC}$ to base) and $R_2=20\,\text{k}\Omega$ (from base to ground)
- Transistor: $\beta=100$, $V_{BE}=0.7\,\text{V}$

Assume $V_T\approx 25\,\text{mV}$ for small-signal and take $r_e\approx \dfrac{V_T}{I_E}$.

Find the DC Q-point $(I_C, V_{CE})$ and the midband voltage gain magnitude $|A_v|\approx \dfrac{R_C}{r_e}$.
